sm: The hosts open with President Trump trying to calm fears after a string of high-profile tech outages. He calls them individual events, says the press is having fun with them, and argues they would have gone unnoticed under the previous administration. He also warns that any country behind an attack would face repercussions. Reporting then covers a JPMorgan Chase breach through third-party vendors that exposed marketing data, with about 16,000 customers leaked by a ransomware group that also claimed Visa and MasterCard leaks. Share prices of all three fell. The NSA's classified internal network stayed partly down for a third day, with no evidence of a cyber attack. Finally, Anthropic debuted on the stock market at 111 dollars 50 a share, 30 percent above its 83 dollar IPO price, at a valuation above 2 trillion dollars, the largest IPO ever. OpenAI is reportedly eyeing its own IPO.

The Army's ninth brigade engineer battalion in Georgia offered re-enlistment incentives, including an extra four day weekend to play the newly released Grand Theft Auto 6. Forty-three soldiers re-enlisted, and some also received bonuses, such as 60,000 dollars for one sergeant. Next, Iowans received a short-notice warning about toxic lead dust from a planned military detonation at a munitions plant, with possible exposure stretching over 50 miles. The International Court of Justice ruled nine to six that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, though it has no way to enforce the ruling. Van Gogh's Blossoming Chestnut Trees sold for over 190 million dollars, a new record for the artist. On Guinness World Records Day, attempts included a father and son parallel parking Minis at once and a portrait of the Statue of Liberty painted in 43.5 seconds. The hosts then recap the day's other stories and say they will return tomorrow morning.
